page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 7.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 0.9 GB of memory per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n1-highcpu-8 delivers modest performance characteristics. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng falls into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is weak, though large block read and write bandwidth reaches average levels. Cryptographic, compression, and text processing tasks show poor to weak results, with single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression ranking in the bottom 10%. However, the server achieves average performance in Geekbench ray tracing and PassMark CPU score metrics.

From a resource density perspective, this instance represents an entry-level compute-focused option within the legacy N1 family. It trades off memory capacity and modern instruction sets, such as AVX-512, to offer a higher vCPU count at a lower resource tier. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a cost-efficient choice for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints, though its older architecture limits its raw processing throughput compared to newer generations.

The n1-highcpu-8 is suited for workloads that require multiple dedicated threads but have minimal memory requirements. Appropriate use cases include basic multi-threaded software compilation, lightweight ray tracing, simple web serving, and text processing tasks that fit within its 7.0 GB memory limit.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-focused server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 7.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. It contains 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, 45 MB of L3 cache, and lacks local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks position this instance in the lower performance tiers, with weak single-core and multi-core CPU results, and poor single-threaded compression speeds. However, it maintains average performance in large-block memory bandwidth and ray tracing. Qualitatively, this server offers a high vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a cost-effective option for legacy multi-threaded applications with low memory footprints. It is best suited for lightweight software compilation, basic web serving, and simple parallel processing tasks.
